concept.title: Home-page layouts
concept.shortdesc: The home page has five layouts; the default chooses one from the map's shape, and govuk.homepage.layout overrides it. Every screenshot below is this manual, rebuilt with a different layout.

conbody.p: home pagelayoutsWith auto (the default): a single top-level entry gives the start layout, two to eight entries give annotated, and more entries — or a bookmap with several chapters, like this manual — give grouped. The grid and accordion layouts are explicit choices, and list keeps a plain contents tree.

section.title: Start
section.p: For a publication that is one linear guide: a green start button leads straight into the first page, with the guide's sections listed beneath.

image.alt: Home page with the title, abstract, a green Start now button, and a contents list of the first sections.

section.title: Annotated contents
section.p: Each top-level entry appears with its short description — write good shortdesc elements and this layout writes itself.

image.alt: Home page listing each entry as a linked heading with a one-line description underneath.

section.title: Grouped sections
section.p: The default for this manual: a heading per chapter with its pages listed beneath, each with a hint-styled description.

image.alt: Home page with chapter headings, each followed by a list of page links with grey description lines.

section.title: Grid
section.p: Chapters side by side in columns — the GOV.UK answer to a tile grid, using typography rather than boxes.

image.alt: Home page with three columns, each a chapter heading, description, and its page links.

section.title: Accordion
section.p: For very large publications: each group collapses behind a toggle, with Show all sections provided by the Design System component. Without JavaScript every section simply shows open.

image.alt: Home page with collapsed accordion sections named after the chapters, each with a Show toggle.
